correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the primary equation (3.21) as Q=m^2 s^k+sum_{j=1}^{m-1} s^e[j+(m-j)s^k][m-tau+tau s], with e=floor((kj-1)/m) and tau=kj-me. For n=kq+r, each exponent block has affine endpoints a(q+1)+floor(ar/k)+1 and (a+1)(q+1)+floor((a+1)r/k), with final endpoint m-1. Summing 1,j,j^2 symbolically proves degree at most three in q; the joint quadratic summands ensure that bound. A separately authored exact rational reconstruction summed these endpoints, rather than interpolating four samples, for all 84 reduced residues at k=7,...,17. Chebyshev conversion gave F=A+qB+((k+r)q^2+(k/3)q^3)H, with H=(2+cos theta)|sum_{j=0}^{k-1}exp(ij theta)|^2>=0. Coefficient identities for q^2,q^3 were checked exactly in every residue. Integer-scaled de Casteljau subdivision at depths 4,6,6,6,7,8,8,8,8,9,9 respectively showed every Bernstein coefficient of A and B exceeds 1/200. Hence F>(1+q)/200 for every q>=0. All phi(k) residues (6,4,6,4,10,4,12,6,8,8,16) are included. Auxiliary direct-formula comparisons at q=0,1,2,3,4,13 check indexing but are not the infinite argument. Reciprocity, degree 2k, nonzero endpoints and strict circle positivity give exactly k roots inside and k outside, counted with multiplicity. Each interior root realizes product coordinates (s,s) using sqrt-modulus domain points; this is not z=w, and the kernel denominator is nonzero.
